summary: Yes, but the improvement is metric-dependent: addressing the ~3:1 class imbalance (via class_weight='balanced' or SMOTE) reliably improves threshold-based, minority-sensitive metrics like F1 (+0.02 to +0.03) and balanced accuracy (+0.05) for both Logistic Regression and Random Forest, mainly by trading precision for a large recall gain on the minority '>50K' class. Threshold-free metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) do not improve and PR-AUC actually drops slightly, so imbalance handling changes the model's operating point/trade-off rather than uniformly improving discriminative quality.
primary_metric_name: F1 delta (Random Forest, class_weight=balanced minus baseline), repeated 5x5 CV mean
direction: balanced > baseline (F1 and balanced accuracy improve; ROC-AUC/PR-AUC roughly flat-to-slightly-worse)
methodological_choices: Dropped 3,620 rows (7.4%) with '?' missing values rather than imputing; encoded target as binary ('>50K'=1); dropped redundant string 'education' column (kept 'education-num'); one-hot encoded 7 categorical columns, standard-scaled 6 numeric columns (including fnlwgt as-is); 80/20 stratified train/test split (random_state=42); compared Logistic Regression and Random Forest (300 trees) under 3 imbalance strategies -- no handling (baseline), class_weight='balanced', and SMOTE oversampling (applied only inside CV training folds via imblearn Pipeline to avoid leakage); evaluated with 5-fold stratified CV plus a single held-out test pass; used F1, balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, minority-class recall/precision as the metric suite since no single metric fully characterizes imbalance effects; chose RF class_weight='balanced' vs. RF baseline as the primary comparison since RF was the stronger base model and class_weight is the most common practical fix (SMOTE gave very similar but slightly weaker results than class_weight in every comparison).
verification_method: Repeated stratified 5-fold CV with 5 different random seeds (25 total fold evaluations, RepeatedStratifiedKFold random_state=123) on the training split, comparing RF baseline vs RF class_weight='balanced' pipelines fit independently per fold; computed mean/std of the paired per-fold metric deltas and a 95% t-interval.
verification_result: Finding held up robustly: F1 improved in 25/25 of the 25 repeated-CV runs (mean delta +0.0228, std 0.0078, 95% CI [0.0195, 0.0260]); balanced accuracy improved consistently too (mean delta +0.0478, 95% CI [0.0455, 0.0500]). The held-out test set independently reproduced the same pattern (F1: 0.7087 vs 0.6827, balanced acc: 0.8271 vs 0.7766, PR-AUC: 0.7943 vs 0.8050, ROC-AUC: 0.9153 vs 0.9170), confirming imbalance-handling gives a real, stable gain on threshold-based/minority-sensitive metrics but a real, stable small loss on PR-AUC, not just a metric-selection artifact.
